corrections.caveats: Own README admits a lower win rate on multi-CCD and Intel mesh hosts. It loses to OpenMP on barrier-bound stencils, to oneTBB on heavy-tailed reductions, and to libfork on recursive fork-join with a multi-CCD pool. In runtime-benchmarks, nqueens (80765 us vs libfork 69010 us) and matmul(2048) (48069 us vs libfork 44140 us) are slower than libfork and TooManyCooks. Peak RSS is higher than its peers' (e.g. fib(39) 44.5 MB vs tbb 11.69 MB). runtime-benchmarks is maintained by the TooManyCooks author (Unlicense), with CPU boost enabled and the schedutil governor. The README's single-CCD Zen 5 'wins the vast majority' claim is qualitative in the text (charts only).

notes: Numbers verified on the runtime-benchmarks README. MIT license and 54 stars confirmed; last_commit was not re-checked.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README headline: often ~3-6x faster than OpenMP and ~12-16x faster than Rayon and Taskflow per parallel-for dispatch. N-body at N=512, us per iteration, static/dynamic: 128x Intel SPR ForkUnion C++ 54/86, ForkUnion Rust 40/67, OpenMP 115/226, Rayon 483/739, Taskflow 666/694. Connected components, GTEPS: 192x Graviton 5 ForkUnion Rust 258.7/87.3, ForkUnion C++ 192.6/77.6, OpenMP 53.9/0.4, Rayon 8.4/6.2, Taskflow 53.0/0.4.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: -O3 -march=native (C++), RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native (Rust), no LTO; compiler names and versions not stated for the tables (the README mentions LLVM and MinGW-GCC on the 24x i9 Windows host)
corrections.caveats: Author-run numbers. CPUs are given as families and core counts, not SKUs, and compiler versions are not stated. The latency win is dispatch overhead; on 24x Intel RPL Windows, OpenMP static beats ForkUnion C++ in connected components (11.4 vs 10.0 GTEPS) and Rayon roughly ties ForkUnion C++ in n-body (151/151 vs 148/143). The 3-6x OpenMP headline is the upper range: the C++ static cell on 128x SPR is 115 vs 54 us (about 2.1x, derived from page data).
